cues.en: Air conditioners are pretty cool.
cues.zh: 空调确实很酷。

cues.en: But there's an increasingly popular variety of them that figuratively and literally sucks. That would be these bundles of joy. Portable air conditioners seem to be taking the world by storm.
cues.zh: 但有一种越来越流行的空调，简直是字面意义和比喻意义上的“吸人”。说的就是这些讨喜的小家伙。便携式空调似乎正在席卷全球。

cues.en: Or at least have taken the air conditioner aisle of the hardware store by storm. But are they any good? Do these cold making machines have what it takes to usurp the traditional window unit? No.
cues.zh: 至少，它们已经席卷了五金店的空调货架。但它们真的好吗？这些制冷机器有能力取代传统的窗式空调吗？不能。

cues.en: Portable air conditioners are actually kinda
cues.zh: 便携式空调其实有点

cues.en: bad.
cues.zh: 糟糕。

cues.en: Now, it's not like they don't work, and some of them aren't quite as bad as most, plus they can really come in handy. This one here is serving duty precisely because the window it's venting through isn't really suited to holding a window unit in place with any sense of confidence.
cues.zh: 倒也不是说它们完全没用，其中一些也没大多数那么糟，而且确实能派上用场。比如这一台之所以在这里工作，正是因为它排风的这扇窗户不太适合稳稳地固定窗式空调。

cues.en: And I know because I tried. Yes, this here is the symbol of my shame. The air conditioner that was never meant to be. But luckily for you, I didn't return it because it's gonna be a great visual aid. Now, in this video, I'm going argue that if you need an air conditioner, you should gravitate towards these simple window units and away from those trendy portable units, if you can.
cues.zh: 我知道这一点，因为我试过。没错，这就是我的羞耻象征。这台本不该存在的空调。不过还好我没把它退掉，因为它会成为很好的演示道具。在这期视频里，我要论证的是，如果你需要空调，只要条件允许，就应该优先考虑这种简单的窗式空调，远离那些时髦的便携式空调。

cues.en: And to find out why,
cues.zh: 要弄清楚原因，

cues.en: we need to learn a little bit about air conditioning. Air conditioners are mechanical devices which collect and concentrate heat energy in order to move it from one place to another. The cold air they create is in fact ordinary air that's had its heat energy sucked right out of it. And of course, we can't just bottle that energy up, though that would be super cool if we could figure that out, so instead we move it somewhere else, usually to outside air.
cues.zh: 我们得先了解一点空调的原理。空调是机械设备，它们收集并集中热能，把热能从一个地方转移到另一个地方。它们制造的冷空气，其实就是热能被彻底抽走的普通空气。当然，我们不能把这些能量直接装瓶保存起来，虽然如果能做到那一定酷毙了，所以我们会把它转移到别处，通常是室外空气中。

cues.en: And inside every air conditioner, you'll find three essential parts that make that happen. This is the basis of nearly every air conditioning and refrigeration system in service today.
cues.zh: 在每台空调内部，你都会发现三个关键部件共同实现了这一过程。这就是当今几乎所有空调和制冷系统的基础。

cues.en: The black cylinder contains a compressor, which squeezes a gas called a refrigerant into a small space, decreasing its volume and increasing the pressure it's under. The high pressure gas, which has now gotten quite hot thanks to the fact that it just got compressed,
cues.zh: 黑色圆柱体内装有压缩机，它将一种称为制冷剂的气体压缩到狭小空间内，减小其体积并提高其承受的压力。这种高压气体由于刚被压缩而变得相当热，

cues.en: travels through these pipes into the second key component, the condenser.
cues.zh: 随后通过这些管道进入第二个关键部件——冷凝器。

cues.en: The condenser is a heat exchanger designed to cool that hot gas down as quickly as possible.
cues.zh: 冷凝器是一种热交换器，旨在尽快冷却这种热气体。

cues.en: The densely spaced fins increase its surface area to speed up the heat transfer,
cues.zh: 密集排列的翅片增加了表面积，以加快热传递，

cues.en: and a fan helps to speed it along even more by blowing air across the fins.
cues.zh: 风扇则通过将空气吹过翅片来进一步加速这一过程。

cues.en: Since the refrigerant is now pressurized,
cues.zh: 由于制冷剂现在处于加压状态，

cues.en: its boiling point has increased.
cues.zh: 其沸点已经升高。

cues.en: And in fact, its boiling point has increased so much that once we get it down to something like a 130 or a 150 degrees,
cues.zh: 事实上，它的沸点升高了很多，以至于当我们把它降到大约130或150度时，

cues.en: it will condense into a liquid.
cues.zh: 它就会凝结成液体。

cues.en: So, as the hot gas winds its way through all these pipes and its heat energy gets transferred to the air, it slowly turns into a liquid, releasing a ton of heat energy as it does so. Now here's where the magic happens. That liquid is being held back by a metering device such as a thermal expansion valve to keep the pressure high in the condenser and limit the amount of liquid refrigerant that can pass through.
cues.zh: 因此，当热气体蜿蜒穿过所有这些管道、其热能传递给空气时，它会慢慢变成液体，同时释放大量热能。接下来就是神奇之处。这种液体被节流装置（如热力膨胀阀）拦住，以保持冷凝器中的高压，并限制可通过的液态制冷剂量。

cues.en: This basic air conditioner uses a capillary tube, a long copper tube with a very small internal diameter, to restrict the refrigerant and thus limit its flow.
cues.zh: 这台基础空调使用毛细管，也就是一根内径很小的长铜管，来限制制冷剂，从而限制其流量。

cues.en: But once it makes it through to the other side, it finds itself in a second heat exchanger called the evaporator.
cues.zh: 但一旦它穿到另一侧，就会进入第二个换热器，叫做蒸发器。

cues.en: This one is functionally identical to the condenser, except the pressure inside here is much, much lower thanks to the suction created by the intake side of the compressor.
cues.zh: 它在功能上和冷凝器完全相同，只不过由于压缩机进气侧产生的抽吸作用，这里的压力要低得多得多。

cues.en: Once inside here, the refrigerant can relax, and its boiling point suddenly shoots way, way down, like into the well below zero territory.
cues.zh: 一旦进入这里，制冷剂就可以放松下来，它的沸点会骤然大幅下降，降到零下很低的区间。

cues.en: And that means it's gonna spontaneously
cues.zh: 这就意味着它会自发地

cues.en: boil, or evaporate,
cues.zh: 沸腾，或者说蒸发，

cues.en: because,
cues.zh: 因为，

cues.en: well, it's too hot for it to remain a liquid. But to change phases back into a gas, it needs to get energy from somewhere, and luckily, the fins of the evaporator help it absorb the energy in the room, and the effect is that the room gets colder. In effect, the heat energy inside the room is being used to warm up the refrigerant as it evaporates.
cues.zh: 嗯，对它来说太热了，无法保持液态。但要重新相变成气体，它需要从某处获取能量，幸运的是，蒸发器的翅片帮助它吸收房间里的能量，结果就是房间变冷了。实际上，房间里的热能正被用来加热蒸发中的制冷剂。

cues.en: Thinking about this can be kinda weird because we like to think of the evaporator as getting cold,
cues.zh: 这么想可能有点反直觉，因为我们习惯认为蒸发器是在变冷，

cues.en: which it is, but it's getting cold because it pulling heat energy out of the air and into the refrigerant inside of it. Coldness is really just less concentrated heat energy, and since heat likes to go towards cold places to spread out, it naturally finds its way.
cues.zh: 它确实在变冷，但它变冷是因为它在把热量从空气中抽走，送进内部的制冷剂里。冷其实只是浓度较低的热能，而热量喜欢流向冷的地方扩散开来，所以它自然会找到路径。

cues.en: With the help of a fan.
cues.zh: 借助风扇。

cues.en: After the refrigerant has absorbed as much energy as it can, it re enters the compressor, where the cycle starts all over again.
cues.zh: 制冷剂吸收尽可能多的能量后，会重新进入压缩机，循环再次开始。

cues.en: Once it's under high pressure, it will be able to condense into a liquid again, releasing the energy it just absorbed to the outside air through the condenser.
cues.zh: 一旦处于高压下，它就能再次凝结成液体，通过冷凝器将刚刚吸收的能量释放到外部空气中。

cues.en: Now, don't want to get too far into the physics of how this works, nor talk about what makes refrigerants special and why they have been and continue to be a notoriously tricky set of chemicals to manage.
cues.zh: 现在，我不想深入探讨其物理原理，也不谈制冷剂有何特殊之处，以及为什么它们一直是一类出了名难管理的化学品。

cues.en: So, all I really need you to know for this video is there's a compressor, a hot side, and a cold side. If we're cooling a room, we want the hot side outside,
cues.zh: 所以，这个视频里我只需要你知道有压缩机、热侧和冷侧。如果我们在给房间降温，我们希望热侧在外，

cues.en: and the cold side inside.
cues.zh: 冷侧在内。

cues.en: Then we can move the heat energy from inside the room to the outside air, cooling the room. So let's take a look at where these components are when the window unit is in operation.
cues.zh: 然后我们就可以把热能from房间内部移到外部空气中，从而冷却房间。那么让我们看看窗式空调运行时这些部件的位置。

cues.en: When resting in a window, the bulk of the machine is actually outside of the space it's cooling. The compressor and condenser are both outside, and thanks to the generous amount of styrofoam insulation,
cues.zh: 当安装在窗户上时，机器的主体实际上位于它所冷却的空间之外。压缩机和冷凝器都在外面，而且 thanks to 大量的泡沫塑料隔热层，

cues.en: we get a pretty good thermal barrier.
cues.zh: 我们得到了相当不错的热屏障。

cues.en: When cooling, none of the actual air in the room is moved outside.
cues.zh: 制冷时，房间里实际的空气一点也不会被移到外面。

cues.en: Only the refrigerant, and thus the heat energy it's absorbed makes it out. This maximizes efficiency.
cues.zh: 只有制冷剂，以及它吸收的热能，会被排出去。这最大化了效率。

cues.en: If you have a central air conditioning system, you probably have what's called a split system.
cues.zh: 如果你有中央空调系统，你可能有所谓的分体系统。

cues.en: Here, the compressor and condenser, along with the cooling fan, are contained in a single unit which sits outside,
cues.zh: 压缩机、冷凝器和冷却风扇都装在一个位于室外的机组里，

cues.en: and copper refrigerant lines are run into the building to a separate evaporator located in an air handler or incorporated in a furnace.
cues.zh: 铜制冷剂管道接入建筑内，连接到单独的蒸发器，蒸发器位于空气处理机中或集成在炉子里。

cues.en: See? It's a split system, as the evaporator and condenser are split apart.
cues.zh: 看到了吗？这就是分体系统，因为蒸发器和冷凝器是分开的。

cues.en: These systems are highly efficient, with the entire hot side located outside and away from the living space, space, and only a tiny hole is required in the home's thermal barrier to move the refrigerant in and out. Alright, and now let's take a look at a portable air conditioner.
cues.zh: 这类系统效率很高，整个热端都在室外、远离生活空间，而且房屋热障上只需开一个小孔让制冷剂进出。好了，现在来看看便携式空调。

cues.en: You may notice that the entire machine is inside.
cues.zh: 你可能会注意到整台机器都在室内。

cues.en: That means not only is the cold side inside,
cues.zh: 这意味着不仅冷端在室内，

cues.en: the hot side is inside, too.
cues.zh: 热端也在室内。

cues.en: Well, that's not great. We want the energy being absorbed by the evaporator and released into the condenser to make its way outside somehow.
cues.zh: 这可不太妙。我们希望蒸发器吸收、冷凝器释放的能量能以某种方式排到室外去。

cues.en: So what do portable air conditioners do? They suck in indoor air through these vents, blow it across the condenser to cool it off, and then push it outside through that hose. That last sentence is very important. They pull in air through these vents, air that they just cooled, mind you, and blow it outside.
cues.zh: 那便携式空调是怎么做的呢？它们通过这些通风口吸入室内空气，吹过冷凝器给它降温，然后通过那根管子排到室外。最后这句话非常重要。它们通过通风口吸入空气——注意，是它们刚刚冷却过的空气——然后吹到室外。

cues.en: That sounds pretty friggin stupid just on its face. Now, it's not like it doesn't work. If these didn't work, they wouldn't be nearly as popular as they are. Also, two hose portable air conditioners, which suck in outside air to cool the condenser and then blow it back out in two separate hoses, are available, but they are an increasingly rare part of the portable air conditioner universe, and the vast majority on sale are single hose units just like this one. So if this machine relies on drawing air in through these vent slots to cool the condenser, and then has to barf the now hot air outside,
cues.zh: 光看表面这听起来就挺蠢的。当然，它不是不能用。要是不能用，也不会这么受欢迎了。另外，双管便携式空调——吸入室外空气冷却冷凝器，再通过两根独立管子排出去——是有的，但它们在便携式空调市场里越来越少见，在售的绝大多数都是像这样的单管机型。所以，如果这台机器靠通过这些通风口吸入空气来冷却冷凝器，然后还得把变热的空气排到室外，

cues.en: that means not only is it sacrificing some of the cool air it just generated,
cues.zh: 这意味着它不仅牺牲了一部分刚产生的冷气，

cues.en: it's also creating a low pressure environment in whatever space it's in. Now, the air pressure outside the room is greater than inside,
cues.zh: 还会在所在空间里形成低压环境。现在房间外的气压高于室内，

cues.en: and that means that outside air is going to make its way in through the walls to replenish the air that just left. You can't just expel air from a room without it getting replaced somehow.
cues.zh: 这就意味着室外空气会穿过墙壁渗进来，补充刚刚排出去的空气。你不可能把空气从房间里排出去而不以某种方式补充回来。

cues.en: Otherwise, you're in a vacuum chamber, and I advise you leave as soon as possible.
cues.zh: 否则，你就像待在真空室里，我建议你尽快离开。

cues.en: And what replaces it is ultimately the hot outside air that you're fighting against. Genius!
cues.zh: 而取代它的，最终是你一直在对抗的室外热空气。真是天才！

cues.en: And thus, we're at the core of this issue. Single hose portable air conditioners will always be significantly
cues.zh: 于是，我们就触及了问题的核心。单软管便携式空调的效率永远会显著

cues.en: less efficient than a window unit because they're not just pulling the heat energy out of your room, they're also pulling the air out, too.
cues.zh: 低于窗式空调，因为它们不仅把热量从你房间里抽走，也把空气抽了出去。

cues.en: In fact, if you go to a hardware store and take a look at a fresh assortment of portable units, you'll often find that they have two cooling capacities listed these days.
cues.zh: 事实上，如果你去五金店看看新到的一批便携式空调，你会发现如今它们常常标出两个制冷量。

cues.en: Why? Well, because newer testing methods are accounting for the losses brought about by this hose. So while the unit may technically be able to move 8,000 BTUs per hour, thanks to the warm air it's drawing back in, as well as its own cold air it's blowing back out, it's effectively only moving 6,000 BTUs per hour.
cues.zh: 为什么？因为更新的测试方法把这条软管带来的损失也算进去了。所以，虽然这台机器技术上每小时能移动 8,000 BTU，但由于它吸回的是暖空气，还把自身的冷空气吹了出去，实际每小时只移动 6,000 BTU。

cues.en: So basically, it's 25% less efficient. But it's actually much worse than that. This little 5,000 BTU window unit consumes 455
cues.zh: 所以基本上，它的效率低了 25%。但实际情况还要糟得多。这台 5,000 BTU 的小窗机耗电 455

cues.en: watts.
cues.zh: 瓦。

cues.en: If we take a look at this 5,500
cues.zh: 如果我们看看这台 LG 的 5,500

cues.en: BTU portable unit from LG,
cues.zh: BTU 便携式空调，

cues.en: you'll see that it uses over a kilowatt.
cues.zh: 你会发现它耗电超过一千瓦。

cues.en: That's more than double the input power required to generate only 10% more cooling.
cues.zh: 这所需输入功率是两倍多，却只换来 10% 的额外制冷量。

cues.en: A window unit that consumes that much power can produce roughly double the cooling capacity.
cues.zh: 耗电这么多的窗式空调，制冷量大约能达到它的两倍。

cues.en: So yeah.
cues.zh: 好吧。

cues.en: Eek.
cues.zh: 呃。

cues.en: Now, I'm not here to say that these are terrible devices and you're a fool if you own one, because I'd be calling myself a fool twice if that were the case. But I will say that in general,
cues.zh: 我不是来说这些设备很糟糕、买了就是傻的，因为如果真是那样，我等于骂了自己两次傻瓜。但我想说，总的来说，

cues.en: these should be your last resort. If you have the option to use a traditional window unit,
cues.zh: 它们应该是你最后的选择。如果你能用传统的窗式空调，

cues.en: take it. It's much more energy efficient,
cues.zh: 就用它。它要节能得多，

cues.en: and it will cost less to run.
cues.zh: 而且运行成本更低。

cues.en: And yeah, I get it. They're ugly. They block your view from the window. They're not exactly attractive from the outside either.
cues.zh: 是啊，我明白。它们很丑。会挡住窗外的视线。从外面看也不怎么好看。

cues.en: But it's not just energy efficiency that they're better at. Air conditioners are noisy.
cues.zh: 但窗式空调更胜一筹的不只是能效。空调还很吵。

cues.en: They're noisy because they're mechanical devices with a buzzy compressor and two droning fans moving air around. With a traditional window unit, the compressor and one of the two fans are outside.
cues.zh: 它们吵，是因为它们是机械装置，有嗡嗡作响的压缩机和两个单调轰鸣、推动空气流动的风扇。传统窗式空调则把压缩机和两个风扇中的一个放在室外。

cues.en: Thanks to that thermal insulation, you get a lot of sound insulation, too. You'll certainly notice a difference when the compressor is on versus when it's not, but it's often pretty subtle. Especially because as is the case for many window units, the same motor drives the indoor blower fan and the condenser fan, so the only part that cycles on and off is the compressor.
cues.zh: 多亏了那层隔热，你也获得了很好的隔音。压缩机开和不开时，你肯定能听出差别，但通常相当细微。尤其是因为，和许多窗式空调一样，同一个电机驱动室内送风机和冷凝器风扇，所以唯一会启停的部件就是压缩机。

cues.en: And of course split systems are even quieter because the loud parts are nowhere near the living space.
cues.zh: 当然，分体式空调还要更安静，因为吵闹的部件根本不在生活空间附近。

cues.en: Compare that to this thing. Not only is the compressor now inside the room you're trying to work or sleep in, but so is the condenser fan. The result is that it's not that noisy when it's only running the circulator fan, but when its thermostat calls for cooling, it gets way, way louder.
cues.zh: 相比之下，看看这个东西。现在不仅压缩机在你工作或睡觉的房间里，冷凝器风扇也在里面。结果是，只开循环风扇时还没那么吵，但一旦温控器要求制冷，它就会吵得多得多。

cues.en: Suddenly, the compressor kicks in, which again is inside the room, and a second fan turns on to expel the heat from the condenser.
cues.zh: 突然，压缩机启动了，它同样位于房间内，接着第二个风扇也转起来，把冷凝器的热量排出去。

cues.en: It's a good thing the condenser fan shuts off when it's not actively cooling, as otherwise it would suck even more air out of the room. But it means there's a stark difference in noise levels between not cooling,
cues.zh: 好在冷凝器风扇在不制冷时会关闭，否则它会从房间里抽出更多空气。但这也意味着不制冷时和制冷时的噪音水平有天壤之别，

cues.en: and cooling.
cues.zh: 和制冷时。

cues.en: And if you're trying to sleep in the same room as one of these, you'll have to put up with it going from pretty quiet to loud as hell, and back over and over again.
cues.zh: 如果你和这么个东西睡在同一个房间，你就得忍受它从相当安静到吵得要命，再回来，反反复复。

cues.en: This is a cheap in house brand unit from that place where you save big money, so I wasn't expecting it to be whisper quiet,
cues.zh: 这是一台来自那个“省钱大卖场”的廉价自有品牌机型，所以我本来就没指望它能静音，

cues.en: but I've also got a more proper unit from LG that, while a little more elegant in the way it handles the transition from cooling to not cooling and vice versa,
cues.zh: 但我也有一台更正规的LG机型，虽然它在制冷与不制冷之间切换的处理上稍微优雅一些，

cues.en: is still much much louder when it's cooling.
cues.zh: 但制冷时还是吵得多得多。

cues.en: I'm a pretty heavy sleeper, and even for me, it can be a challenge to ignore the thing and fall asleep.
cues.zh: 我睡觉很沉，但即便如此，对我来说，忽略这东西入睡也是个挑战。

cues.en: And another thing to consider is that while window units steal a bigger chunk of your windows, they don't steal your floor space. Portable units aren't small, and they can't sit flush against the wall thanks to the hose, so be prepared to rearrange a little furniture.
cues.zh: 还有一点要考虑：虽然窗式机占用你窗户的面积更大，但它们不占你的地面空间。便携机可不小，而且因为有软管，没法紧贴墙壁，所以准备好挪动一些家具吧。

cues.en: And by the way, that hose? It gets hot. That heat energy it just concentrated isn't gonna go away without a fight, and since this hose isn't insulated at all, some of it's coming right back into the room. Fantastic.
cues.zh: 顺便说一句，那根软管？它会变热。它刚刚集中起来的热能不会轻易消失，而且这根软管完全没有隔热，所以一部分热量正直接回到房间里。太棒了。

cues.en: But I'll admit, portable AC units are handy.
cues.zh: 但我得承认，便携式空调确实很方便。

cues.en: Really handy. They don't need proper installation like a window unit does, which is quite a pain I might add. They can easily be moved from room to room thanks to the wheels they're on,
cues.zh: 真的很方便。它们不像窗式空调那样需要正规安装，顺便说一句，安装窗式空调可真是件麻烦事。它们底部装有轮子，可以轻松地从一个房间推到另一个房间，

cues.en: that's why they call them portable,
cues.zh: 这就是它们被称为便携式的原因，

cues.en: and they fit window types that might otherwise be unable to accommodate an air conditioner, such as vertical windows or even patio doors. You can even run them through a small dedicated vent if you choose.
cues.zh: 而且它们能适配那些原本无法安装空调的窗户类型，比如垂直窗甚至庭院门。你甚至可以选择通过一个小型专用通风口来排气。

cues.en: But sadly, their single hose design makes them, honestly,
cues.zh: 但遗憾的是，它们单软管的设计使得它们，说实话，

cues.en: a terrible device when it comes to efficiency.
cues.zh: 在效率方面表现很差。

cues.en: I'd like to see more double hose units available for sale. They're still gonna have the noise and floor space disadvantages,
cues.zh: 我希望市面上能买到更多双软管机型。它们仍然存在噪音和占地空间的缺点，

cues.en: but they at least regain much of their efficiency back.
cues.zh: 但至少能恢复大部分效率。

cues.en: Last year I tried a portable mini split system with a separate outdoor compressor and condenser unit, and an indoor evaporator unit connected via a flexible refrigerant hose.
cues.zh: 去年我试了一款便携式迷你分体系统，它有独立的室外压缩机和冷凝器单元，以及通过柔性制冷剂软管连接的室内蒸发器单元。

cues.en: Sadly, my unit had a refrigerant leak and stopped working after a few weeks.
cues.zh: 遗憾的是，我那台机器出现了制冷剂泄漏，几周后就停止工作了。

cues.en: It looks like that's a common problem, but let me tell you, it was blissful while it worked. Quiet, efficient, and effective.
cues.zh: 看起来这是个常见问题，但让我告诉你，它工作时真是种享受。安静、高效、效果好。

cues.en: I'd like to see this product get more development, but I also understand that it's got way more limitations than even a window unit. Unless you want to get creative with some sort of exterior wall bracketing,
cues.zh: 我希望这个产品能得到更多开发，但我也明白它的局限性甚至比窗式空调还大。除非你能想出某种外墙支架的创意方案，

cues.en: this is limited to a Ground Floor room or a room with a balcony or something similar. But anyway, if we're gonna keep using these things, can we please get more dual hose units? I get that they're less flexible particularly with vertical or narrow windows, and so are probably less desirable,
cues.zh: 否则它只能用于一楼房间或有阳台之类的房间。但话说回来，如果我们还要继续使用这些设备，能不能请多出一些双软管机型？我知道它们灵活性较差，尤其是在垂直窗或窄窗上，所以可能不太受欢迎，

cues.en: but hopefully with more people aware of the energy losses caused by continuously pushing air out of your home,
cues.zh: 但希望随着更多人意识到持续将室内空气排到室外所造成的能量损失，

cues.en: we'll see increased demand.
cues.zh: 我们会看到需求增加。

cues.en: Still, if you're looking for an air conditioner in a situation where a window unit could work,
cues.zh: 不过，如果你在那种窗式空调就能搞定的场合需要一台空调，

cues.en: you're seriously better off going with the window unit. Contrary to what you might think, portable units certainly not an upgrade.
cues.zh: 那你还真不如选窗式空调。和你想的相反，便携式空调绝对算不上升级。

cues.en: Other than their portableness. That's that's pretty cool.
cues.zh: 除了便携性之外。那确实挺酷的。

cues.en: Thanks for watching, and I hope you found this video to be as cool as a correctly charged air conditioning system.
cues.zh: 感谢观看，希望你觉得这个视频和制冷剂充注正确的空调系统一样酷。

cues.en: I do want to explore air conditioning a little more, because I find it fascinating.
cues.zh: 我确实想再多研究研究空调，因为我觉得它很迷人。

cues.en: The way that we exploit the physical properties of certain gases to make heat energy move where we want it to go is kinda mind blowing.
cues.zh: 我们利用某些气体的物理特性，让热能移动到我们想要它去的地方，这种方式有点令人惊叹。

cues.en: Oh, and by the way, not all refrigerants are crazy complex
cues.zh: 哦，顺便说一下，并不是所有制冷剂都是极其复杂的

cues.en: chemicals. Some small refrigerators and air conditioners are starting to be charged with propane.
cues.zh: 化学物质。一些小冰箱和空调开始使用丙烷充注了。

cues.en: Propane, also known as r two ninety, is becoming an increasingly common refrigerant thanks to its abundance and relative environmental harmlessness.
cues.zh: 丙烷，也叫 R290，正变得越来越常见，因为它储量丰富且相对对环境无害。

cues.en: Unfortunately,
cues.zh: 不幸的是，

cues.en: it's also flammable, which makes servicing these little tricky, and makes it unsuitable for larger units which need a lot of refrigerant.
cues.zh: 它也是易燃的，这让维修这些小设备变得棘手，也让它不适合需要大量制冷剂的大型机组。

cues.en: But especially for small cheap units like these things that are likely to simply be disposed of when they die rather than actually serviced, it's a great opportunity to use it. This machine, though, while it is charged with a flammable refrigerant, uses difluromethane
cues.zh: 但对于像这些小而便宜的设备来说——它们坏了之后很可能直接被丢弃而不是真正维修——使用它是个很好的机会。不过这台机器虽然充注的是易燃制冷剂，用的却是二氟甲烷
